UPSTREAM: soc/intel/apollolake: bootblock: implement platform_prog_run() Once bootblock copied romstage into CAR it may not jump into it right away. This is because we are in NEM mode, there is no backing store and a miss in L1 may cause L1D line snoop that gets written back. The solution is to flush L1D to L2 so snoop guaranteed to hit L2. CHROMIUM: ath10k: Add adjacent wlan radio interference detecting interface Some platforms integrate several radios together. When one radio wants to spectral scan the current channel, the adjacent radio's activity will introduce some interference in the spectral scan result. To combat the problem, enable the FW to set a special mark within the spectral scan results. Using such a mark, the user who is processing the data can identify whether the data has been introduced by the interference of the adjacent radio during that period. The user can interpret more accurate spectral scan results with the given marks where interference occurred. This technique requires the preconditions that the scanning and adjacent radio have some physical connection to make them aware of each other's activity from within the FW layer, and the FW claimed supporting this capability. to enable this feature, execute: echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc Then run the spectral scan steps. To check whether the spectral scan data be interfered, execute: cat /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc INTERFRC DETECT FOR SPEC SCAN: Enable/Disable 5G_interference: X/0 2G_Interference: X/0 X means the interference number in the scan period, 0 means no interference. These counters will be reset when next round spectral scan be triggered BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran iperf after connecting a wifi client with our AP (cherry picked from commit f3262e6d20cf91ad964b565128a6e16976e01cf2) (source: wireless-3.18) Change-Id: I9259717906406b30e3ee4ab2cbdc7c2137d8f5a1 Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Mohammed Shafi Shajakhan <mohammed@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340720 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: Ignore the adjacent radio's activity when surveying a channel The overall goal for a scanning radio is to evaluate the outside radio environment. Some platforms integrate several radios together. When one radio wants to survey the current channel, the adjacent radio's activity will make this survey result inaccurate. Switcher can be used to enable the FW to ignore the survey time slot when the adjacent radio is active, especially for TX. This skipped scan approach will make the survey result more accurate. This technique requires a precondition that the scanning and adjacent radio have some physical connection to make them aware of each other's activity from within the FW layer, and the FW claimed supporting this capability. BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran traffic with wifi client connected echo 2 > /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc Then run the survey scan and dump the stastics: iw dev wifiX survey dump The TX&RX counter showed already deducted the time slot be interfered To check whether the feature is enabled, execute: cat /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/ath10k/adjacent_wlan_interfrc INTERFRC DETECT FOR SURVEY SCAN: Enable/Disable (cherry picked from commit 825defe22caa71caa1e69b1234967d2e66319952) (source: wireles-4.2/kernel v3.14) Change-Id: I2478e1939d8934f57c980ecc8e8037433fc43dae Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Mohammed Shafi Shajakhan <mohammed@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340722 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ath10k: Supply the 64bits channel survey counters The previous TX & RX cycle counters used to report the channel survey are 32 bits, it will wraparound after reach 0xffffffff, the wraparound happens in a short cycle (24 seconds), if the user wants survey > 24 seconds TX & RX counters on a specific channel, the counters will overflow again and again which make the long time survey impossible. There is a new WMI message be added to access the counter in 64bits format, it will greatly extent the overflow time, and userspace will have enough time to handle such case by calculate the counter difference between two samples. The userspace application could call the NL80211_CMD_GET_SURVEY to get the 64 bits counter survey result of currently channel, the result also can be gotten via the available command "iw station survey dump" known limitation: 1: Not be tested for multichannel support scenario 2: Background scan at hostapd AP mode need verificaiton BUG=chrome-os-partner:51964 TEST=ran iperf traffic with wifi client connected The userspace application could call the NL80211_CMD_GET_SURVEY to get the 64 bits counter survey result of currently channel, the result also can be gotten via the available command "iw station survey dump"a (cherry picked from commit 002c1d21718ec37ee298d978b6c1bf62586fe905) (source: wireless-4.2/v3.14) Change-Id: I9065d0f4671e374ad06e1953b83e354509b3eeb2 Signed-off-by: Yanbo Li <yanbol@qca.qualcomm.com> Signed-off-by: Mohammed Shafi Shajakhan <mohammed@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/340723 Commit-Ready: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Tested-by: Yixiang Li <yixiang@google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: ALSA: hda - Skip ELD notification during system suspend The recent addition of ELD notifier for Intel HDMI/DP codec may lead the bad codec connection found as kernel messages like below: Suspending console(s) (use no_console_suspend to debug) hdmi_present_sense: snd_hda_codec_hdmi hdaudioC0D2: HDMI status: Codec=2 Pin=6 Presence_Detect=1 ELD_Valid=1 snd_hda_intel 0000:00:1f.3: spurious response 0x0:0x2, last cmd=0x206f2e08 snd_hda_intel 0000:00:1f.3: spurious response 0x0:0x2, last cmd=0x206f2e08 .... snd_hda_codec_hdmi hdaudioC0D2: HDMI: ELD buf size is 0, force 128 snd_hda_intel 0000:00:1f.3: azx_get_response timeout, switching to polling mode: last cmd=0x206f2f00 snd_hda_intel 0000:00:1f.3: No response from codec, disabling MSI: last cmd=0x206f2f00 snd_hda_intel 0000:00:1f.3: azx_get_response timeout, switching to single_cmd mode: last cmd=0x206f2f00 azx_single_wait_for_response: 42 callbacks suppressed This seems appearing when the sound driver went to suspend before i915 driver. Then i915 driver disables HDMI/DP audio bit and calls the registered notifier, and the HDA codec tries to handle it as a hot(un)plug. But since the driver is already in the suspended state, it fails miserably. As this is a sort of spurious wakeup, it can be ignored safely, as long as it's delivered during the system suspend. OTOH, if a notification comes during the runtime suspend, the situation is different: we need to wake up. But during the system suspend, such a notification can't be the reason for a wakeup. This patch addresses it by a simple check of the current sound card status. The skipped notification doesn't matter because the HDA driver will check the plugged status forcibly at the resume in return. Then, why the card status, not a runtime PM status or else? The HDA controller driver is supposed to set the card status to D3 at the system suspend but not at the runtime suspend. So we can see it as a flag that is set only for the system suspend. Admittedly, it's a bit ugly, but it should work well for now. Reported-and-tested-by: "Zhang, Xiong Y" <xiong.y.zhang@intel.com> Fixes: 25adc137c546 ('ALSA: hda - Wake the codec up on pin/ELD notify events') Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v4.3+ Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de> (Cherry-picked from 8ae743e82f0b86f3b860c27fc2c8f574cf959fd0) From v4.4 BUG=chrome-os-partner:48057 TEST=With the whole series applied the following tests should pass: TEST=No Display artifacts when browsing.
